Sandbox/network confirmation absent (empty scan of tools/environments/); MCP elicitation present but fires mid-tool-call, so the row excludes it). daemon_capability: incapable - these dialogs reach neither sensor: they write no message row so watcher.go's message_count-growth reconcile emits nothing (the session never even leaves ready), and hermes' _fire_approval_hook has six call sites, all on dangerous-command approval paths, none of them a CLI modal. driver_capability: ready - the modals take typed text + Enter and the hermes driver already has slash + send.

assessment.body:
## Verdict

agent_supports: yes (three of the row's four triggers are present in hermes 0.19.0; the fourth is cited as an empty scan)
daemon_capability: incapable (a tool-less dialog reaches NEITHER of this adapter's two sensors: it writes nothing to state.db, and hermes fires no lifecycle hook when one opens)
driver_capability: ready (the modals are answered by typed text through the normal composer + Enter, and the hermes driver already carries `slash` and `send`)

## agent = yes — which triggers, which not

The row names four triggers and asks which the agent under test supports. All
four were checked.

**Trigger 4 — an auto-mode or settings review the product raises before it
proceeds: PRESENT, three separate modals.** Each is a blocking
`_prompt_text_input_modal` overlay (`cli.py:8120`) rendered by the CLI itself,
with no tool call in flight and, for the first two, no model call at all:

- `_confirm_destructive_slash` (`cli.py:10838-10922`) — raised by `/clear`,
  `/new`, `/reset` and `/undo` before they discard conversation state. Default
  ON: `approvals.destructive_slash_confirm` is `True` in the shipped schema
  (`hermes_cli/config.py:2774`).
- `_confirm_and_reload_mcp` (`cli.py:~10924-10990`) — raised by `/reload-mcp`
  before invalidating the provider prompt cache, gated by
  `approvals.mcp_reload_confirm`.
- `_confirm_expensive_model_switch` (`cli.py:8382-8412`) — an "!!! Expensive
  Model Warning !!!" raised before applying a costly `/model` switch.

**Trigger 2 — a first-use trust prompt for a configured server: PRESENT.**
`agent/shell_hooks.py:736-757` blocks on `input("Allow this hook to run?
[y/N]: ")` the first time a hook declared in `~/.hermes/config.yaml` is
registered, recording consent to `~/.hermes/shell-hooks-allowlist.json`.
Bypassable only via `--accept-hooks` / `HERMES_ACCEPT_HOOKS=1` /
`hooks_auto_accept`. It fires at CLI startup, before any session exists.

**Trigger 3 — a server-driven MCP elicitation: PRESENT BUT OUT OF SCOPE FOR
THIS ROW.** hermes implements `elicitation/create` (`tools/mcp_tool.py:1652+`
`ElicitationHandler`, passed to `ClientSession` as `elicitation_callback`),
routed to a blocking modal through `tools/approval.py:3867
request_elicitation_consent`. But in hermes it is the SDK's mid-tool-call
callback — the class docstring says so ("ask the client to collect structured
input from the user mid-tool-call") and the handler replays
`owner._pending_call_context`, the agent context captured by the MCP tool
wrapper. An MCP tool call is therefore open across the whole dialog, so this
one belongs to the tool-carried class 2.19/2.26 covers and the row explicitly
excludes it. It is not used as this cell's trigger.

**Trigger 1 — a sandbox or network-access confirmation: ABSENT.** Empty scan,
stated so it is not re-litigated: `grep -n 'input(\|prompt_dangerous\|confirm'`
over every backend in `tools/environments/` (base, local, docker, singularity,
modal, managed_modal, daytona, ssh, file_sync) returns nothing — the container
backends prompt for nothing, and `_should_skip_container_guards`
(`tools/approval.py:2863`) shows isolation REMOVING prompts rather than adding
one. A tree-wide grep for `network access` / `network_access` finds only SSRF
guards that block silently (`tools/browser_tool.py:3459`). The one startup
posture check, `hermes_cli/security_audit_startup.py`, states in its own first
line that it is "warn-on-load, never blocks".

## daemon = incapable — both sensors are silent on the entry edge

This adapter has TWO sensors, and this is the part that has changed since 2.19
was assessed on this column (that cell says "hermes installs no hooks in this
PR"; it now does). Neither carries a tool-less dialog.

### 1. The store carries nothing, and the session never even leaves `ready`

`agent.go` declares `Source: agent.ProcessOwnedStore{PathForPID: ... StorePath()}`
— the shared `$HERMES_HOME/state.db`, opened through `core/pkg/sqlitero`
(`metrics.go:72`). `watcher.go` emits `EventActivity` only when a session's
`message_count` GROWS (`watcher.go:44`, `:282`, `:416`).

The slash-confirm and model-switch modals run entirely inside `cli.py` on the
slash-command path — no LLM call, no tool call, no message row. So
`message_count` does not move, the watcher emits nothing at all, and the
session sits at whatever state it already had. There is no `working` for a
`waiting` to interrupt, let alone a `waiting`: the row's very first assertion,
`ready -> working`, is unproducible. The hook-consent prompt is worse still —
it blocks at hook registration, before `hermes chat` has written the `sessions`
row (which this column's own 2-1 and 2-17 specs record as arriving only on the
first user message), so no session exists to transition.

### 2. The hook channel is real, and none of these dialogs fires it

This adapter installs `pre_approval_request`, `post_approval_response` and
`on_session_end` (`hookinstaller.go:232-236`), and `hooks.go` maps them to
`HandlePermissionPromptHook` / `ReleasePermissionPromptHold` /
`HandleStopHook`. That gives hermes a genuine `waiting` state — for the
approval path.

hermes' `_fire_approval_hook` (`tools/approval.py:96`) has exactly six call
sites: `:154` and `:162` (the smart-approval observer pair, `surface="smart"`),
`:3099` and `:3167` (inside `_await_gateway_decision`, `surface="gateway"` or
`"mcp-elicitation/<server>"`), and `:3576` / `:3592` (around
`check_all_command_guards`' CLI prompt, `surface="cli"`). Every one of them is
on a dangerous-command approval path. None of the three CLI modals, and not the
hook-consent `input()`, is on any of them — they call
`_prompt_text_input_modal` or bare `input()` and fire nothing. Even the CLI
MCP-elicitation path fires nothing: `request_elicitation_consent` calls
`prompt_dangerous_approval` directly (`approval.py:3933`), bypassing the hook
pair that `check_all_command_guards` wraps its prompt in; only the GATEWAY
elicitation path fires, via `_await_gateway_decision`, and this adapter
deliberately drops gateway-minted session ids (`sessionIDShape`,
`TestHookReceiver_GatewaySurfaceApprovalIsQuiet`).

Widening the search to hermes' whole roster does not help. `VALID_HOOKS`
(`hermes_cli/plugins.py:135`) is 23 events at v0.19.0, and the only one that
fires anywhere near this class is `on_session_reset` (`cli.py:7491`) — which
fires AFTER the user answers a `/new` or `/reset` confirm, i.e. a
release-side-only signal with no entry counterpart, and which this adapter does
not install.

So the entry edge into `waiting` has no representation on either sensor. That
is `incapable` (the sensor does not exist), not `bug` (a trace the daemon
mis-handles) — the same verdict aider, gemini-cli and antigravity reached on
this row for three different underlying reasons.

## driver = ready

Unlike 2.19, this cell needs no `keys` primitive.
`_prompt_text_input_modal`'s docstring says the modal "lets the normal Enter
key binding submit the typed or highlighted choice", and
`_normalize_slash_confirm_choice` (`cli.py:8253-8284`) accepts typed answers —
`1`/`once`/`approve`/`yes`/`y`/`ok`, `2`/`always`/`remember`,
`3`/`cancel`/`no`/`n`. The hermes driver declares
`DRIVE_ELICITS="send slash sleep wait_turn"` (`driver-interactive.sh:125`), so
the trigger is a `slash` step and the answer is a `send` step. No primitive is
missing.

This is recorded so that if the sensor gap ever closes, nobody re-derives a
driver gap that is not there. It is derived from the modal's typed-text path
and has never been driven live — see `caveats`.

## Route

agent=yes, daemon=incapable -> **frozen** (`of status` renders `unobservable`).
Recipe `applicable: false`, matching the frozen siblings on this row (aider,
gemini-cli, antigravity).

## What would unblock it

A hermes-side event fired when a non-approval modal OPENS. hermes already has
the shape — `pre_approval_request` / `post_approval_response` are observer-only
and bracket the approval prompt exactly the way this row needs — so the ask is
that the CLI's other blocking modals fire the same pair (or a sibling event)
with `tool_call_id` unset, which `_fire_approval_hook` already threads through
as a contextvar (`approval.py:115-116`). That is an upstream request, not
irrlicht work: this adapter's receiver would need no change beyond recognising
the event name.
caveats: VACUOUS-PASS CONDITION, and it is an ENVIRONMENT PROPERTY: both slash modals are self-disabling. Answering 'Always Approve' persists approvals.destructive_slash_confirm: false (cli.py:10915) or approvals.mcp_reload_confirm: false to config.yaml, permanently. A host where either was ever answered that way runs the recipe with NO modal at all - the slash command executes straight through, the session never leaves ready, and a spec that only asserted 'final state ready' would go green having tested nothing. If this cell is ever unfrozen, `hermes config get approvals.destructive_slash_confirm` must be re-probed at record time and asserted true as a precondition, and the recipe must answer 'once', never 'always'.

SECOND VACUOUS-PASS CONDITION: if a future recipe reached for hermes' MCP elicitation as the trigger, the cell would collapse into 2.19/2.26's tool-carried class - an MCP tool call is open across that whole dialog (tools/mcp_tool.py's ElicitationHandler is the SDK's mid-tool-call elicitation_callback and replays owner._pending_call_context), so both edges ARE carried by a tool call and the row's central claim goes untested while every phase passes. The trigger must stay one of the CLI's tool-less modals.

daemon=incapable is derived from source plus this adapter's code, NOT from a recording - no hermes tool-less modal has been driven under a recording daemon (this verb runs none). It rests on three independently checkable facts rather than a plausible mechanism: (1) the slash/model modals run in cli.py with no LLM or tool call, so sessions.message_count never grows and watcher.go's reconcile emits nothing; (2) _fire_approval_hook has six call sites, all on dangerous-command approval paths, and none of the modals is on any of them; (3) of hermes' 23 VALID_HOOKS only on_session_reset fires near this class, and only AFTER the answer. If any of the three changes upstream, re-assess rather than trust this.

driver=ready has never been exercised: it is read off _prompt_text_input_modal's typed-choice path and _normalize_slash_confirm_choice's alias table, not off a live run. One unmodelled detail to check before relying on it - the driver's send_text appends a trailing Enter 0.4s after the literal text, which is exactly how the modal is submitted, but a second stray Enter landing in the composer after the modal closes would post an empty turn. Verify before the first live drive.

agent_supports=yes rests on trigger 4 (three CLI modals) and trigger 2 (the shell-hook trust prompt). Trigger 2 is the weaker of the two for THIS row even though it is a textbook tool-less dialog: it blocks before hermes has written a sessions row, so a recording of it has no session to attach the arc to. Trigger 4 is the one a recipe would use. Trigger 1 is cited as an empty scan; trigger 3 is present but excluded by the row's own definition.

No observations block is asserted. of verify hard-asserts only against the newest recording's replay-golden summary (internal/validate/observations.go:141-160); hermes' Parser sets only ev.ModelName (parser.go:78) and the store-derived token lift is gated adapter == antigravity (cmd/replay/metrics.go:59), so tokens_nonzero and cost_nonzero can never pass on this column - verified here independently, and matching what this column's 2-17 cell recorded after seeing both pins red. A model pin would be a doc-guess on a cell that is never recorded.

2.19's daemon=incapable on this column is now stale on one point - it was written when this adapter installed no hooks. That does not change THIS cell (the modals reach the hook channel no more than they reach the store), but 2.19 itself is worth re-assessing and would likely land daemon=full for the `terminal` gate.

sources.note: The three tool-less modals. _prompt_text_input_modal (8120) renders a blocking prompt_toolkit overlay and its docstring states the normal Enter binding submits the typed or highlighted choice. _confirm_expensive_model_switch (8382-8412) raises the 'Expensive Model Warning' before a /model switch. _confirm_destructive_slash (10838-10922) guards /clear, /new, /reset and /undo, and persists approvals.destructive_slash_confirm: false at 10915 when the user answers 'always'. _confirm_and_reload_mcp (from ~10924) guards /reload-mcp, modal at 10958. _normalize_slash_confirm_choice (8253-8284) is the alias table (1/once/approve/yes/y/ok, 2/always/remember, 3/cancel/no/n) that makes these answerable by typed text. Line 6534 enumerates the CLI's blocking modal states: _sudo_state, _secret_state, _approval_state, _slash_confirm_state, _clarify_state. Line 7491 fires on_session_reset - AFTER the confirm resolves.

Line 2774: approvals.destructive_slash_confirm defaults to True in the shipped schema, which is what makes trigger 4 a default-on surface rather than an opt-in one. The same block carries hooks_auto_accept: False (2811), the flag that would suppress trigger 2's prompt.

Lines 736-757: the first-use trust prompt for a config-declared shell hook - 'Hermes is about to register a shell hook that will run a command on your behalf' followed by a blocking input('Allow this hook to run? [y/N]: '), recorded to ~/.hermes/shell-hooks-allowlist.json by _record_approval (760). Trigger 2, and a genuinely tool-less blocking dialog - but raised before any session row exists.

ElicitationHandler (from 1652): hermes implements MCP elicitation/create, passing the handler to ClientSession as elicitation_callback. Its docstring says elicitation collects input 'mid-tool-call' and the handler replays owner._pending_call_context, the agent context captured by the MCP tool wrapper - which is why this trigger is PRESENT but excluded from this row: an MCP tool call is open across the dialog, so both edges are tool-carried.

_fire_approval_hook (96) and its complete call-site set: 154/162 (smart-approval observer, surface=smart), 3099/3167 (_await_gateway_decision, surface=gateway or mcp-elicitation/<server>), 3576/3592 (around check_all_command_guards' CLI prompt, surface=cli). All six are dangerous-command approval paths. request_elicitation_consent (3867) calls prompt_dangerous_approval directly at 3933 on the CLI path, firing NO hook. _should_skip_container_guards (2863) shows sandbox isolation removing prompts rather than raising one.

VALID_HOOKS at 135 - the 23 lifecycle events hermes v0.19.0 offers. Read in full: the only event that fires near a tool-less modal is on_session_reset, which fires after the answer. There is no open-a-dialog event of any kind, which is the upstream gap the 'what would unblock it' section names.

EMPTY SCAN for trigger 1 (sandbox / network-access confirmation): grep for input(, prompt_dangerous and confirm across base.py, local.py, docker.py, singularity.py, modal.py, managed_modal.py, daytona.py, ssh.py and file_sync.py returns nothing. The container backends raise no confirmation of any kind. Cited so a future audit does not re-litigate the negative.

The one startup posture review, and its own first line rules it out as a trigger: 'Startup security posture audit (warn-on-load, never blocks)' - it emits logger.warning records and 'never raise or block startup'.

installedHookEvents (232-236): pre_approval_request, post_approval_response, on_session_end, against minHermesVersion 0.19.0 (275). The header documents that hermes' 23 events come in three subscription mechanisms and that the shell-hook route is the one used. This is the sensor that did not exist when 2.19 was assessed, and checking it is why this cell's incapable verdict is a statement about which hermes call sites fire rather than about there being no channel.

The receiver: pre_approval_request -> HandlePermissionPromptHook (the waiting assertion), post_approval_response -> ReleasePermissionPromptHold, on_session_end -> release + HandleStopHook. sessionIDShape rejects gateway-minted ids (8 hex vs the CLI mint's 6), which is what also drops the one elicitation path that DOES fire a hook - the gateway one.

reconcile() emits EventActivity only when a session's message_count grows (44, 282, 416). A modal that writes no message row produces no event at all, so the session cannot even reach `working` - the row's first assertion. This is the store half of the incapable verdict.

Source: agent.ProcessOwnedStore{PathForPID: StorePath()} - the single shared $HERMES_HOME/state.db is the adapter's only file-tier Source, opened through core/pkg/sqlitero (metrics.go:72), with `store` and `hooks` as its two declared permissions. There is no third sensor.

Line 125: DRIVE_ELICITS="send slash sleep wait_turn". Both primitives a slash-confirm recipe needs are present; keys, interrupt, reset_session and the rest are still not_implemented (513-521) but this cell's recipe would not need them - which is what separates its driver verdict from 2.19's gap:keys.

The nearest sibling verdict (agent=yes, daemon=incapable, driver=ready): gemini raises a dozen tool-free dialogs but its NotificationType enum has one member and fireNotificationEvent one caller, so the entry edge has no representation. Read for shape; hermes reaches the same place by a different route (no event of any kind fires when its modals open).

The other frozen sibling, and the closest analogue to hermes' trigger 2: agy's workspace-trust gate blocks before agy mints the conversation dir, so no session exists yet. hermes' shell-hook consent prompt has exactly that shape, which is why trigger 4 rather than trigger 2 is the one a recipe would use.

recipe.notes: daemon_capability=incapable - hermes' tool-less modals write nothing to $HERMES_HOME/state.db and fire none of hermes' 23 lifecycle hooks, so no driver step sequence can make the waiting episode observable; the session does not even reach `working`. WHEN UNFROZEN by an upstream event fired when a non-approval modal opens, the recipe is: interactive `hermes chat`; a precondition re-probe that `approvals.destructive_slash_confirm` is still true (answering 'always' once disables it permanently - see caveats); one `send` of a plain prompt so a real store-backed session exists and a turn boundary is on record; a `slash` step of `/undo` (the least destructive of the four guarded commands, and the one that does not rotate the session id the way /new and /reset do); a `sleep` of >=15s while the modal is held open so the waiting episode is visible; a `send` of the literal `1` to answer 'Approve Once' (never 'always'); then `wait_turn` and a trailing `sleep` of >=15s for the settle. Every primitive it needs - send, slash, sleep, wait_turn - is already in DRIVE_ELICITS, so unlike 2.19 no driver work is required.
